doc.title: Tom Scott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 1, 2022 [interview 1 of 2]

title: First TV composing job: The Bold Ones via Stanley Wilson, and Dave Grusin
summary: Universal's Stanley Wilson hired him to score an episode of The Bold Ones; he also befriended Dave Grusin in the Howard Roberts Quintet.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: From your quote resume, it looks like you weren’t just happy with being a saxophone player. I mean by that that you have film credits and conducting and arranging. Did that all develop about in the same time?

Well roughly. I mean here’s what happened. The first, if I remember this correctly, the first job that I was offered to write an episode of a television show was Universal. The music supervisor at Universal was a guy named Stanley Wilson, a friend of my father’s, they had worked together, there are probably pictures, years ago. But I was sort of, you know, getting a reputation as this guy, this musical guy, and I had written a couple of tunes for Emil Richards, kind of odd time tunes and other things. I don’t remember exactly how Stanley Wilson came to believe that I would be, that I would work as a T.V. composer but he believed it for whatever reason, and hired me to do an episode of a thing a series, it was called “The Bold Ones.” And it was actually three separate series that kind of rotated every week. There was a doctor and a lawyer and a cop. Something like that. And I did one of them, I don’t even remember which one it was now. But that was the beginning. So once you do a movie, or one show, that’s a credit. And so now you have a credit and so that gives you some more, you know I don’t want to say “clout,” but it’s certainly more credibility as a film and television composer, and then of course I befriended Dave Grusin. I played with him at Donte’s. He played piano with the Howard Roberts Quintet. It was me and Howard and Dave, John Guerin, and Chuck Domanico. And it was a wonderful, wonderful band. And Dave was a great guy and I guess he recognized my abilities as well. So it was a show for Quinn Martin Productions. Quinn Martin Productions, back in those days, dominated prime time television shows.
